title: Compatibility ledger, pin-exemption workflow, and acceptance tests for model-catalog entries
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Clarify and codify the runtime compatibility ledger, a lightweight pin-exemption workflow for short-lived/experimental open models, and a focused acceptance-test suite that the runtime and catalog teams can run to approve entries. This ticket collects PRD-level requirements, acceptance criteria, trade-offs, and handoff artifacts for implementation by Engineering.
background: We onboard more community models with diverse forks and quantized variants. Current intake documents describe pinning and compatibility at a high level but teams still escalate runtime mismatches and emergent rollbacks. We need a prescriptive ledger and a pin-exemption flow (soft-entry) that makes risk explicit, enables automated sanity tests, and provides clear rollback triggers.
scope: Define schema for the compatibility ledger (fields and semantics), define pin-exemption eligibility and lifecycle (duration, approval path, telemetry requirements), author a concise acceptance-test list (runtime sanity checks, perf thresholds, KV/batching compatibility), and produce handoff artifacts (PRD, example ledger entries, test scripts).
out_of_scope: Full implementation of ledger storage API, complete UI for catalog console, or automatic rollback automation. Those will be separate ENG and Console tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Compatibility ledger schema specified with at least these fields: model_id, variant_tag, declared_compatibility_level, runtime_notes, recommended_quantization_profiles, expected_max_seq, pin_required_flag, soft_entry_expiry_days, responsible_team_contact

A2: Pin-exemption workflow documented with roles, approval gates, and telemetry requirements (must include failure-rate and latency delta thresholds and required eval prompt set), and an example approval ticket flow

A3: A 10-test acceptance suite defined (plain-text generation smoke, kv-cache warm/restore, continuous-batching stress, quantized-run matching threshold, edge-case prompt set) with pass/fail criteria and how to surface results to Console
A4: Risk classification rubric created (none/low/medium/high) mapping to allowed soft-entry durations and required approvals
A5: A minimal handoff package produced: PRD doc link, sample ledger JSON for three model variants (stable, soft-entry, flagged), and a GitHub path for the acceptance-test harness
A6: Sign-off recorded from runtime lead (ENG), security/compliance, and product owner before moving to ENG implementation backlog
success_metrics: Fewer than 2 unplanned rollback incidents for soft-entry models in first 90 days after rollout
50% reduction in developer/ops escalations related to runtime incompatibility for newly onboarded open models within quarter
All new model entries include a ledger record at time of catalog registration
deliverables: Pin-exemption playbook (approval checklist and telemetry requirements)
Acceptance-test list + test definitions and example scripts
Handoff checklist and proposed ENG/Console tickets list

tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Favor a lightweight JSON ledger attached to catalog entries rather than a heavy new database service to minimize iteration friction
Trade-off: Short soft-entry windows reduce risk but increase operational overhead for teams needing longer evaluation; we propose tiered durations based on risk classification
Decision: Require automatic telemetry ingestion for soft-entry approvals but defer full rollback automation to a follow-up project
implementation_notes: Engineering will need clear read/write contract for ledger attachment to catalog entry, runtime hooks to run the acceptance-test harness on onboarding, and tracing instrumentation to measure latency/failure deltas. Provide example payloads and a small mock harness used for initial validation.

notes: This PRD is intentionally lightweight to accelerate adoption. If pilot metrics show unstable behavior we will pause and convert the soft-entry flow to a stricter pinned intake with longer vetting. Maintain conservative defaults until telemetry is verified.
